chapter_title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ...
spiritual_reading:
Inner perception is first drawn up from a more interior level into conscious expression; then discerning intelligence unfolds it into an ordered form; then judgment distinguishes and separates what is fitting from what is not; then the outer understanding gathers it into a coherent utterance adapted to reception; and finally the ultimate form fixes it as something complete for communication. Thus a meaning comes forth through a sufficient complement of operative powers and enters the external plane where it can be perceived by others.

In the same way, a truth intended for mutual life is brought from what is unformed into what is usable through a sufficient series of distinct operations: one power brings the matter of it into a state fit for formation, another strengthens it by confirmed assent, another sets it into right proportion as it is carried into outward form, another impresses upon it a determinate quality and authority from its ruling love, and another removes what is mixed and impure so that it may be clean in its ultimate presentation. By these sufficient operations a truth is shaped and made attractive, and then it enters common life. It becomes something that can be appropriated, held, communicated, and exchanged in use.

So it is with all communicated meaning: it is first formed inwardly and then made suitable for reception through a sufficient complement of operative powers, until it comes forth into external perception and is taken up by the understanding of others.

fills.fill: The mouth takes it and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips gather it!
fills.notes: The sequence is a correspondential inventory of five operative instruments by which what is interior becomes utterance in ultimates. The missing opening must name the first member that receives and contains what will be articulated, i.e., the mouth, completing the fivefold series that culminates in hearing outside.

assessment: Nearly all gaps are trivial mid-word restorations with fixed readings. The only substantive lacuna (¶1 #1) is constrained by the correspondential fivefold anatomy of utterance; restoring “The mouth takes it” completes the series in the impersonal, technical register of the oldest substrate.
